# Coverage ratchet baseline (#127) — per-package merged
# (unit + integration) coverage floors in percent, enforced by
# scripts/coverage-ratchet.sh in the Coverage workflow.
#
# Rules:
#   - Raise a floor in the same PR that earns the improvement.
#   - Never lower a floor without a recorded decision in the PR body.
#
# Seeded from the v0.9.0 published numbers (RELEASE_NOTES.md).
#
# v1.0.0 recorded decision (release PR #154):
#   - pkg/udhcpc 81.3 -> 85.5: RAISED, earned by the v6 client-args
#     and BuildEvent table tests this cycle.
#   - pkg/plugin 82.4 -> 77.5: LOWERED deliberately. v1.0.0 added a
#     large amount of new defensive/error-path code to this package
#     (renew() re-address failure arms, awaitLinkLocal timeout, the
#     macvlan MAC pin error path, the v6 setupClient arm, ifname
#     threading through Join/CreateEndpoint). The new *behaviors* are
#     covered by the expanded integration + failure-injection suites;
#     the residual gap is `if err != nil { log }` branches that need
#     fault injection not feasible at integration level. Measured
#     78.0; floor set at 77.5 for epsilon room. The intent is to
#     ratchet this back up as error-path coverage is added, not to
#     normalize the lower number.
#   - pkg/util 87.7 -> 87.0: LOWERED for run-to-run integration
#     variance only — no util code changed this cycle; measured 87.1,
#     0.1 over the old epsilon. New floor leaves variance headroom.
#
# v1.2.0 recorded decision (PR #220, #206 — error-path coverage):
#   - pkg/plugin 77.5 -> 82.0: RAISED. This is the follow-through on the
#     v1.0.0 intent above. New docker-client interface + netlink
#     function-var seams made the previously integration-only / wholly
#     unreachable error arms unit-testable (netOptions fallback,
#     recoverEndpoints, lookup/initialDHCP/reacquire docker arms,
#     validateParentForChild, deleteParentAttachedEndpoint, addRoutes,
#     findLinkByMAC). Measured merged 82.3; floor 82.0 for epsilon room.
#     Restores the pre-v1.0.0 level (was 82.4).
#   - pkg/util 87.0 -> 88.0: RAISED, earned by the JSONErrResponse
#     log-severity branch tests. Measured 88.7; floor 88.0.
#   - pkg/udhcpc / cmd/net-dhcp left at floor: their +0.3/+0.4 this run
#     is integration run-to-run variance, not earned by this PR (no
#     udhcpc/cmd code or tests changed) — not ratcheted.
#
# v1.3.0 (#245): pkg/udhcpc → pkg/dhcp and cmd/udhcpc-handler →
#   cmd/dhcp-handler (post-dhcpcd misnomer rename, no code change).
#   Floors carry over unchanged under the new import paths; the
#   historical decision notes above keep the names they had at the
#   time. Same code, same floors.
#
# v1.3.1 recorded decision (#303 — reconcile floors with measured):
#   The pkg/dhcp and cmd/dhcp-handler floors were still the carried-over
#   udhcpc-era numbers; the dhcpcd migration (#152) and the v1.3.0 test
#   work earned coverage on top that no PR ratcheted in, leaving up to
#   25 points of silent-regression headroom. Measured merged coverage
#   (Coverage runs #22 + #23, identical to 0.1%):
#   - pkg/dhcp 85.5 -> 89.5: RAISED. Measured 90.0; 0.5 under.
#   - cmd/dhcp-handler 50.0 -> 74.0: RAISED. Measured 75.0; 1.0 under
#     because the package is one ~16-statement main() and granularity
#     is coarse.
#   - pkg/plugin 82.0 -> 83.5: RAISED. Measured 83.8; 0.3 under, the
#     same margin the v1.2.0 decision used for this package.
#   - pkg/util (88.7 meas.) and cmd/net-dhcp (75.4 meas.) left at
#     floor: their deltas are within the documented variance band,
#     not earned by any identifiable change.
#
# v1.3.1 (#305, PR #306): pkg/plugin 83.5 -> 83.8. RAISED, earned by
#   the state-persistence error-arm tests (saveOptions/saveTombstones
#   CreateTemp + Rename injection). Measured merged 84.1 on this PR's
#   coverage dispatch; all other packages identical to the decimal
#   across four runs now, so the +0.3 is attributable, not variance.
#   Floor 0.3 under measured, same margin as the prior two decisions.
# v1.3.5 (#338, PR #349): pkg/util 88.0 -> 95.0. RAISED, but NOT earned
#   by this cycle — the gap was already there and went unclaimed. Dev
#   measured 88.7 on 2026-07-05 (coverage run 28738787076) and 95.5 the
#   same day (run 28753476811); the jump came with the #317 ptrace fix
#   (d652519), which let the plugin enter non-root netns and so made
#   util's Await* poll paths actually execute. Stable at 95.5 across
#   every run since, including v1.3.4's release measurement. Deferred
#   from the v1.3.4 release PR to avoid another serialized coverage run
#   on an otherwise-ready release. Floor set 0.5 under measured, the
#   same margin as the decisions above.
#
#   pkg/plugin deliberately NOT raised: it measured 83.4 against a floor
#   of 83.8 at v1.3.4, holding only via the 0.5 ratchet epsilon. The
#   DeleteEndpoint tests in this PR are the first repayment (that
#   handler went 0% -> 72.7% unit, and its not-found arm is unreachable
#   from the integration suite, so it should move the merged number too
#   — unlike the v1.3.4 lifecycle tests, which duplicated paths
#   integration already covered and moved it 83.3 -> 83.4). Re-measure
#   at the release PR and raise only what the number supports.
#
# v1.4.0 recorded decision (#364, measured on Coverage run 30656054736
#   against dev at 3f0998c):
#   - cmd/net-dhcp 75.0 -> 76.0: RAISED. Measured 76.4, the same number
#     the v1.3.5 release measured, so the +1.4 has been stable across two
#     cycles and is not variance. Earned by the OUTAGE_TICK / OUTAGE_GRACE
#     duration parsing added to main.go in #357 actually being exercised.
#     Floor 0.4 under measured, the margin this file uses elsewhere. This
#     is the raise #364 deferred from the v1.3.5 release PR; deferring it
#     a third time would make "deferred" a synonym for "untracked".
#   - pkg/plugin 83.8 -> 84.5: RAISED. Measured 85.0. This is the one
#     worth reading twice: the package was deliberately LOWERED to 77.5
#     at v1.0.0 with a recorded intent to ratchet it back, and the
#     v1.3.5 entry noted it holding at 83.4 against a floor of 83.8 on
#     ratchet epsilon alone while predicting the DeleteEndpoint tests
#     would be "the first repayment". Measured 84.0 at that release and
#     85.0 now. The repayment is real and continuing; this cycle's
#     error-path work (#373, #376, #383, #401, #402, #408) is what moved
#     it. Floor 1.0 under measured rather than the usual 0.3-0.5, on
#     purpose and once: #407 and #409 add plugin code AFTER this
#     measurement, and a floor that blocks the release PR over a
#     tenth of a point costs more than the headroom it protects. Tighten
#     it back at the next release, when the number has settled.
#   - pkg/util 95.0, pkg/dhcp 89.5, cmd/dhcp-handler 74.0 left at floor.
#     Measured 98.5, 89.9 and 75.0. dhcp's +0.4 and dhcp-handler's +1.0
#     are the documented variance band on packages nothing touched this
#     cycle. util's 98.5 against a 95.0 floor is a genuine 3.5 of
#     unclaimed headroom, but it moved for the same reason it moved at
#     v1.3.5 — Await* poll paths executing more, not util tests being
#     added — so it is claimed when a change earns it, not because the
#     number is there. Revisit at the next release.
#
# v1.5.0 recorded decision (measured on Coverage run 30811078284, the
#   release PR's own run against dev at 019dba4):
#   - pkg/plugin 84.0 -> 85.0: RAISED, and the margin tightened back to
#     0.5 as the v1.4.0 entry above said to do at this release.
#     Measured 85.5. v1.4.0 set the floor 1.0 under measured on purpose
#     and once, because #407/#409 were landing after that measurement;
#     that reason has expired. Earned this cycle by new code arriving
#     with its own tests rather than after them — endpoints.go (+43),
#     network.go (+38), parent_attached.go (+61), plugin.go (+61)
#     against instance_id_test.go (+103), join_attach_slow_test.go
#     (+157), parent_attached_test.go (+97), state_test.go (+55).
#   - cmd/net-dhcp 76.0 -> 77.5: RAISED. Measured 77.9, floor 0.4 under.
#     Earned by #420: log.go is 31 new statements and arrived with
#     log_test.go, 65 lines of them. v1.4.0 measured 76.4, so this is a
#     +1.5 attributable to an identifiable change, not drift.
#   - pkg/dhcp (89.9) and cmd/dhcp-handler (75.0) left at floor. Neither
#     package has a non-header diff this cycle, and both measured the
#     same numbers at v1.4.0.
#   - pkg/util LEFT AT 95.0, and this cycle says why the earlier
#     decisions were right to leave it. v1.4.0 measured 98.5 and noted
#     3.5 of unclaimed headroom. It measures 96.2 now — DOWN 2.3 points
#     with no util change beyond an SPDX header. That swing is more than
#     four times RATCHET_EPSILON, so util's number tracks how much the
#     integration suite happens to exercise its Await* poll paths, not
#     what its tests cover. Claiming that headroom would have failed
#     this release. Do not raise this floor on a measurement alone; it
#     needs a change that earns it.
#
# v1.8.0 recorded decision (measured on Coverage run 32455281413 against
#   dev at 3b64ee6, dispatched rather than taken from the release PR so
#   the numbers describe what the release actually contains):
#
#   Read this entry as the answer to the three cycles above it. No floor
#   moved at v1.6.0, v1.7.0 or v1.7.1, while the ratchet printed "raise
#   the floor" on every package on every run. The v1.4.0 entry warned
#   that deferring a third time would make "deferred" a synonym for
#   "untracked"; that is precisely what happened. Two floors move here,
#   and the three that do not each say why, so the next reader inherits
#   a decision rather than a silence.
#
#   - pkg/plugin 85.0 -> 86.8: RAISED. Measured 87.3, floor 0.5 under,
#     the margin this file uses. Nine commits touched this package and
#     every one arrived with its own tests: the tombstone store and the
#     six renew phases extracted with unit tests over their guards
#     (#643), the recovery compare-and-set plus its registry tests
#     (#679), server preference and deny lists (#111), and metrics.go
#     with a reflection test asserting every health field reaches the
#     exposition (#651). This continues the repayment the v1.0.0 entry
#     asked for when the floor was deliberately dropped to 77.5.
#   - cmd/net-dhcp 77.5 -> 77.8: RAISED. Measured 78.3, floor 0.5 under.
#     Worth reading twice, because this package is the reason the run
#     above exists. #651 wired METRICS_ADDR into main() and the package
#     FELL to 76.5 — below its floor — because main() is executed only
#     by the cover plugin during the integration suite, and that plugin
#     does not set METRICS_ADDR. The gate caught a real hole: the
#     endpoint shipped with its listener covered and the switch in front
#     of it covered by nothing. #685 answered it with tests rather than
#     a lowered floor, and the package now measures 78.3 — above the
#     77.9 it held before the feature landed.
#   - pkg/dhcp LEFT AT 89.5, measured 90.1. #111 did add code here with
#     tests (dhcpcd.go +36, dhcpcd_servers_test.go +87), so this is not
#     the usual "nothing changed" case. It is left because the headroom
#     is mostly wobble: the same tree measured 89.9 on 2026-08-20 (run
#     32384008443) and 90.1 today, so 0.2 of the 0.6 is run-to-run. A
#     floor at 89.6 would buy 0.1 of real protection and add a way for a
#     future release to fail on noise. Raise it when a change earns
#     something worth the epsilon.
#   - cmd/dhcp-handler LEFT AT 74.0, measured 75.0 — the same 75.0 it has
#     measured at every release since v1.3.1, with no commit touching the
#     package this cycle. The v1.3.1 entry already recorded why the
#     number is coarse: it is one ~16-statement main(), so a single
#     statement is worth about six points. A floor of 74.5 protects
#     nothing that 74.0 does not, because any real regression here is a
#     six-point fall, not a half-point one.
#   - pkg/util LEFT AT 95.0, measured 96.2. The v1.5.0 entry settled
#     this: the number tracks how hard the integration suite happens to
#     exercise its Await* poll paths, not what its tests cover (98.5 at
#     v1.4.0, 96.2 at v1.5.0 and again now, with no util change beyond a
#     header and one error-message line). Do not raise it on a
#     measurement alone.
#
# v1.8.0 second decision (measured on Coverage run 32516336590 against
# dev at 79d4d2f, dispatched after the security-review PRs #693/#694/#695
# landed):
#
#   ONE floor moves, and the two that look like they should are the
#   point of this entry.
#
#   - pkg/dhcp 89.5 -> 89.9: RAISED. Measured 90.4, against an observed
#     band of 89.9 (2026-08-20) / 90.1 / 90.4 -- so this is 0.3 above the
#     top of the band, not inside it, which is what the previous entry
#     said to wait for. Earned by #695: replacing DHCPClientOptions'
#     netns PATH with a borrowed descriptor deleted the GetFromPath
#     error arm and the ns.Close() error arm from client.go, both of
#     which the integration suite never reaches. Floor 0.5 under
#     measured. Note what this raise is and is not: uncovered code was
#     REMOVED, no test was added. That still earns the floor -- the
#     package genuinely has less unexercised surface than it did -- but
#     it is not the same currency as the pkg/plugin raises above.
#
#   - pkg/plugin LEFT AT 86.8, measured 86.9. It FELL: it measured 87.3
#     at the v1.8.0 decision and 87.2 on 2026-08-21. #694 and #695 both
#     arrived with unit tests, so the dip is not untested code in bulk
#     -- it is a handful of new error arms that neither lane can reach.
#     The clearest is the netns_pid_mismatches increment in
#     dhcpManager.Start: unit tests cannot enter Start (it needs a live
#     Docker), and the integration suite never produces a PID mismatch,
#     so the counter's own increment is executed by nothing. This is the
#     #651 shape again -- a guard shipped with the thing it guards
#     covered and the guard itself covered by nothing -- and it is
#     recorded here rather than fixed because closing it needs a seam in
#     Start, which is a change of its own. The floor stays where it is;
#     at 0.1 of headroom the ratchet epsilon (0.5) is what is actually
#     holding this package, and that is worth knowing before the release
#     PR runs.
#
#   - pkg/util LEFT AT 95.0, measured 95.7 -- DOWN from 96.2, in the
#     cycle where util's least-covered function was deleted. #695
#     removed AwaitNetNS along with its untested arms, which raised the
#     package's UNIT coverage 92.3 -> 92.8 measured locally; the merged
#     number went the other way regardless. That is the third
#     independent confirmation of the rule the v1.5.0 entry wrote down:
#     this number tracks how hard the integration suite happens to
#     exercise the Await* poll paths, not what the tests cover. A raise
#     to 95.5 on the 96.2 reading would have failed this run.
#
#   - cmd/net-dhcp LEFT AT 77.8, measured 78.3 -- identical to the
#     v1.8.0 measurement, with no commit touching the package since.
#   - cmd/dhcp-handler LEFT AT 74.0, measured 75.0, as at every release
#     since v1.3.1. The v1.8.0 entry gives the reason: one ~16-statement
#     main(), so a real regression here is a six-point fall.
#
# 2.0 (branch 2.0.0): FOUR PACKAGES, NOT FIVE.
#
# cmd/dhcp-handler is DELETED on this branch. It was the hook binary
# dhcpcd exec'd on every state change, and 2.0 has no dhcpcd: the
# library reports state changes on a Go channel from lease.Manager, so
# there is no process to exec and no argv to parse. Its row is removed
# rather than left at 74.0 because the ratchet fails on a baselined
# package that VANISHED, which is the correct behaviour and would
# otherwise turn a deliberate deletion into a red gate on every run.
#
# The two moving floors are pkg/plugin (86.8) and pkg/dhcp (89.9). Both
# packages changed shape rather than size: pkg/dhcp lost the dhcpcd
# process supervisor, the mount/unshare/FIFO path and the RA guard and
# gained a chassis over the library plus the durable record; pkg/plugin
# lost the outage watchdog, the orphan sweep and the refusal counters.
# Neither floor is RAISED here. This number is measured with the
# integration lane's covdata and the integration lane cannot run
# locally, so a raise written from a local unit run would be a floor
# nobody measured -- and the v1.5.0 and #695 entries above are two
# recorded cases of the merged number moving opposite to the local one.
# Read the measured values off this branch's first green coverage run
# and raise then, in the same PR, if they hold.
github.com/claymore666/docker-net-dhcp/pkg/util 95.0
github.com/claymore666/docker-net-dhcp/pkg/plugin 86.8
github.com/claymore666/docker-net-dhcp/pkg/dhcp 89.9
github.com/claymore666/docker-net-dhcp/cmd/net-dhcp 77.8
